summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of CNS B-cell lymphoma and diabetes insipidus was admitted for his 32nd cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. The infusion was completed without complications, and he received leucovorin rescue starting 24 hours later. Methotrexate levels decreased appropriately, falling to undetectable by discharge. Mild hyponatremia (sodium 132) was noted, attributed to overuse of desmopressin in the setting of aggressive hydration, and was discussed with the patient. He remained neurologically stable with no seizures or focal deficits. Temozolomide was restarted per outpatient regimen. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue all medications, attend a follow-up brain MRI, and schedule his next methotrexate in four months.
problems: Unspecified B-cell lymphoma, extranodal and solid organ sites
